raw_response:
I farm only 10.1 mu, and at my age I do not want to gamble too much. What worked in the village still matters most to me. Wheat and maize are the steady pair here, so I will keep most land in wheat-maize rotation for grain and income, and keep a smaller piece in cotton because cotton can still bring cash if the price is decent. Since there are only 2 people in the house and some family labor goes off-farm, I need simple timing and not too many extra field passes. I have a well, so I can irrigate when the crop really needs it, but pumping costs money, so I will not water too often unless the weather stays dry.

For wheat, I will sow on time in October like usual, use improved seed from the local dealer, put most fertilizer at the start, and save one topdressing for spring if the stand looks weak or yellow. After wheat harvest, I will plant summer maize quickly on the same land, because the turnaround is short and I cannot delay. For cotton, I will keep inputs moderate. Cotton takes more watching and more hand work, so I cannot put too much area there. I would rather use round, familiar rates than push too hard and spend money I may need later.
